cd /private/var/folders/kp/vdv61pd97vd0x29b257r8h7h0000gn/T/barcode-kok6p7e9; cat > /private/tmp/claude-501/-private-var-folders-kp-vdv61pd97vd0x29b257r8h7h0000gn-T-barcode-kok6p7e9/924c60bc-485d-4a05-bb7a-aca5d6f60b53/scratchpad/c.py <<'EOF'
import numpy as np,subprocess
from PIL import Image
b=np.array(Image.open('barcode.png').convert('RGB')).astype(float).mean(0)
N=len(b)
for L in 'ABCDEFGHIJ':
    raw=subprocess.run(['ffmpeg','-v','quiet','-i',f'videos/{L}.mp4','-vf','scale=16:9','-r','2','-f','rawvideo','-pix_fmt','rgb24','-'],capture_output=True).stdout
    f=np.frombuffer(raw,np.uint8).reshape(-1,144,3).mean(1)
    idx=np.linspace(0,len(f)-1,N).astype(int)
    v=f[idx]
    print(L,np.abs(v-b).mean())
EOF

I compared the barcode against all ten videos. For each one, I took frames at regular points through the video, reduced each frame to its average color, and lined them up with the barcode's stripes in order. Then I measured the average color difference per stripe (0–255 scale, lower is closer):

| Option | Difference |
|---|---|
| **C. Rockabye** | **8.2** |
| J. Faded | 22.6 |
| G. Chandelier | 23.7 |
| H. Something Just Like This | 27.3 |
| F. Lean On | 28.0 |
| B. Stressed Out | 28.7 |
| E. Party Rock Anthem | 30.8 |
| A. Blank Space | 34.4 |
| D. Not Afraid | 37.4 |
| I. Closer | 44.4 |

Rockabye's difference is about a third of the next-best video's, so the match is clear. Its dark grey-teal colors line up with the barcode from start to finish.

Answer: C
